**RE: Member appeal of adverse benefit determination dated 2026-08-04**
- **Member:** Rowan Grant
- **Member ID:** W574273539
- **Reference number:** POC-B9867C3E93-20631
- **Denied service:** Total shoulder replacement, CPT 23472
- **Governing policy:** Cigna CMM-318 Shoulder Arthroplasty/Replacement/Revision V1.0.2026 — https://www.evicore.com/sites/default/files/clinical-guidelines/2026-04/Cigna_CMM-318%20Shoul%20Arthro%20Replace%20Revision%20Arthro_V1.0.2026_Eff08.04.2026_Pub04.20.2026.pdf

---

## What I am asking for

I am appealing Cigna's denial of coverage for my total shoulder replacement (CPT 23472), issued on 2026-08-04 under reference number POC-B9867C3E93-20631. The notice states that the requested procedure does not meet the plan's criteria for medical necessity. I am asking Cigna to reconsider and approve this procedure.

My reason is straightforward: the plan's own published criteria in Cigna CMM-318 Shoulder Arthroplasty/Replacement/Revision V1.0.2026 describe the imaging findings, the symptom duration, and the failed non-surgical care that support this surgery — and my medical records document each of those things. My surgeon, Okafor, MD, of orthopedic surgery, submitted this request and documented the findings set out below.

I am submitting this appeal well within the 180-day window described in the notice. The notice states that my appeal must be received by **2027-01-31**.

---

## The plan's criteria, matched to my records

### 1. Imaging findings

The policy states:

> "Radiographic imaging and/or advanced diagnostic study (i.e., MRI, CT) correlates with the individual's reported symptoms and physical exam findings and is conclusive for advanced destructive degenerative joint disease (i.e., osteoarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, avascular necrosis) with marked joint space narrowing and ANY of the following findings:"

The list that follows in the policy includes:

> "◦ irregular joint surfaces ◦ glenoid sclerosis ◦ glenoid osteophyte changes ◦ flattened glenoid ◦ cystic changes in the humeral head"

My records match this. My shoulder radiographs of 2026-05-21 (true AP and axillary views) show **complete loss of glenohumeral joint space with osteophytes, subchondral sclerosis and a flattened glenoid**. A flattened glenoid is one of the findings the policy itself names. Complete loss of joint space is the most advanced form of joint space narrowing there is. CT confirms an intact rotator cuff.

These findings also correlate with what I feel and what my exam shows, as the criterion requires. My exam documents **glenohumeral crepitus, active forward elevation limited to 90 degrees, and external rotation limited to 10 degrees**, with cuff strength intact.

### 2. Function-limiting pain for at least three months

The policy states:

> "Symptoms include function-limiting pain (e.g., loss of shoulder function which interferes with the ability to carry out age-appropriate activities of daily living and/or demands of employment) for at least three (3) months duration"

My records document **9 months of progressive pain in the shoulder, unrelieved by rest** — three times the duration the plan asks for. The loss of function is documented as well: I **cannot reach overhead, cannot dress without help, and cannot sleep on the affected side**. Dressing and sleeping are exactly the kind of daily activities the criterion refers to.

### 3. Failure of non-surgical management for at least three months

The policy states:

> "Failure of provider-directed non-surgical management for at least three (3) months' duration"

and describes that management as:

> "any provider-directed non-surgical treatment, which has been demonstrated in the scientific literature as efficacious and/or is considered reasonable care in the treatment of shoulder pain. The types of treatment involved can include, but are not limited to, the following: relative rest/activity modification; supervised physiotherapy modalities and therapeutic exercises; prescription and non-prescription medications; assistive devices; and/or injections."

My records document the following provider-directed non-surgical treatment:

| Type of treatment | What my records show |
|---|---|
| Prescription and non-prescription medications | **NSAIDs for 4 months with inadequate relief** |
| Injections | **Corticosteroid injection on 2026-03-23, giving 3 weeks of partial relief** |
| Supervised physiotherapy modalities and therapeutic exercises | **Supervised physical therapy focused on range of motion and periscapular strengthening, 2026-04-12 to 2026-06-21, 16 visits completed**, documented in the physical therapy discharge note |

Measured from the injection on 2026-03-23 through the end of physical therapy on 2026-06-21, my provider-directed non-surgical management spans about three months, and my NSAID course alone ran four months. My pain is described in the records as progressive and unrelieved by rest. This is failed non-surgical management, documented as such.

### 4. Other factors in my chart

My records also note **no active infection, no untreated substance use, BMI 29, and non-smoker**.

---

## A request about the criteria that were applied

The excerpts above are the policy language I have. Cigna CMM-318 contains additional criteria that were not reproduced in what I was able to obtain, so I cannot address every element of the policy point by point. The denial notice tells me that the request did not meet the plan's criteria for medical necessity, but it does not tell me **which** criterion was not met.

If Cigna continues to deny this request, I ask that the plan identify, in writing, the specific criterion or criteria in Cigna CMM-318 Shoulder Arthroplasty/Replacement/Revision V1.0.2026 that my records were found not to satisfy, and the specific document or finding the reviewer relied on. That would let me respond to the actual reason rather than to a general statement.

I also ask that this appeal be reviewed by a physician with training in orthopedic surgery, and that the full prior authorization packet from Okafor, MD — including the 2026-05-21 radiograph report, the CT report, the physical therapy discharge note, and the office notes documenting my exam and function — be placed in front of that reviewer.

---

## What I am asking Cigna to do

Please overturn the determination dated 2026-08-04 and approve coverage for total shoulder replacement, CPT 23472, as requested by Okafor, MD.

The plan's policy describes a flattened glenoid with marked joint space narrowing; my radiographs show complete loss of joint space with a flattened glenoid. The policy describes function-limiting pain of at least three months; my records show nine months, with documented loss of overhead reach, dressing, and sleep. The policy describes failure of provider-directed non-surgical management of at least three months' duration, including medications, injections, and supervised physiotherapy; my records document all three, without lasting relief.

I would be glad to provide any additional records the reviewer needs. Please contact me at [my phone number] or [my email address], and please copy Okafor, MD on the determination.

Thank you for taking a careful second look at this.

Sincerely,

**Rowan Grant**
Member ID: W574273539
Reference number: POC-B9867C3E93-20631
